Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.picker

Class PickerFreezeService

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.picker.PickerFreezeService
public final class PickerFreezeService extends Object
Server-owned picker mob freezing: a picker-targeted mob is held NoAi=true while edited and restored to its pre-picker value when released. Owning this on the server (reached via PickerFreezePacket) is what lets a remote client use the picker — and what guarantees the forced flag is undone even when that client disappears.

Robustness, in layers:

  • Live records — one per editing player (FROZEN_BY_PLAYER); freezing a new mob releases the player's previous one, logout (onPlayerLoggedOut(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer)) releases it too, and server stop (onServerStopping(net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer)) restores everything synchronously before the final save. A mob already frozen by another player is refused, since a second capture would read the forced value as the original.
  • Persistent marker — PREV_NO_AI_TAG on the mob holds the pre-picker value for as long as the freeze is live, so an autosave + hard crash (or the mob's chunk unloading mid-edit) can't strand the forced NoAi: on the mob's next join (onMobJoin(net.minecraft.world.entity.Mob)) a stale marker is restored and stripped, while a still-live edit is re-asserted.

All state is transient and single-threaded: every entry point runs on the server thread, reached from packet handlers and server lifecycle events.
